# Comparing data - Practice Test - Year 9

Attempt all questions and show your working. Suggested time: 30 to 35 minutes.

## Section A: Consolidating (Questions 1-4)

**Question 1**

Each table shows a data set as it would appear on a dot plot. Describe the shape of each one as symmetric, positively skewed, negatively skewed or bi-modal.

(a)

| Value | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 4 | 2 | 1 |

(b)

| Value | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 9 | 7 | 4 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

(c)

| Value | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 1 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 5 | 1 |

(d)

| Value | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 5 | 8 | 9 |

**Question 2**

For the data set $12, 15, 9, 25, 15, 18, 11$, find:

(a) the mean

(b) the median

(c) the mode

(d) the range

**Question 3**

Which term (symmetric, positively skewed, negatively skewed or bi-modal) best describes each distribution?

(a) Scores on a very easy test: most students scored high marks and only a few scored low marks.

(b) Weekly incomes in a town: most people earn low or middle amounts and a few earn very large amounts.

(c) The times customers arrive at a café during the day, which is busy at breakfast and again at lunch, and quiet in between.

(d) The total shown when two dice are rolled many times, where 7 is most common and totals further from 7 are less common, by equal amounts on each side.

**Question 4**

The stem-and-leaf plot shows the ages of people at a work meeting. Key: $4 \mid 2$ means 42 years.

| Stem | Leaf |
|---|---|
| 3 | 1 4 8 |
| 4 | 2 5 5 7 |
| 5 | 0 3 6 |
| 6 | 1 |

(a) How many people were at the meeting?

(b) Find the median age.

(c) Find the range of the ages.

## Section B: Standard (Questions 5-16)

**Question 5**

The back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot shows the test scores of two classes. Key: $7 \mid 2$ means a score of 72 for either class.

| Class A leaves | Stem | Class B leaves |
|---|---|---|
| | 4 | 5 9 |
| 8 2 | 5 | 3 6 |
| 7 4 1 | 6 | 0 2 4 6 |
| 8 5 2 0 | 7 | 1 4 |
| 3 | 8 | 8 |
| 1 | 9 | |

(a) How many students are in each class?

(b) Find the median score for each class.

(c) Find the range of the scores for each class.

(d) Which class performed better overall? Use your answers to explain.

**Question 6**

Two basketball players recorded their points in their last six games.

Ari: 12, 15, 18, 14, 16, 15

Ben: 4, 28, 9, 25, 6, 18

(a) Find the mean number of points for each player.

(b) Find the range for each player.

(c) The coach needs a player who scores consistently. Who should she choose? Explain.

**Question 7**

Two groups of Year 9 students recorded how many hours of screen time they had on a Saturday. The results are shown as a parallel frequency table.

| Hours | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Group X | 1 | 4 | 7 | 5 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Group Y | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 6 | 5 | 2 |

(a) How many students are in each group?

(b) Describe the shape of each distribution.

(c) Find the median number of hours for each group.

(d) Compare the two groups in one sentence.

**Question 8**

The times taken by 25 people to complete a puzzle are shown in a grouped frequency table.

| Time (minutes) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| 0 to less than 5 | 2 |
| 5 to less than 10 | 9 |
| 10 to less than 15 | 3 |
| 15 to less than 20 | 2 |
| 20 to less than 25 | 8 |
| 25 to less than 30 | 1 |

(a) Describe the shape of the distribution.

(b) Suggest a reason why the data might have this shape.

**Question 9**

The prices of the last seven houses sold in two suburbs are shown, in thousands of dollars.

Suburb P: 650, 700, 720, 750, 780, 800, 2950

Suburb Q: 700, 720, 760, 790, 810, 830, 850

(a) Find the mean and median price for each suburb.

(b) Describe the shape of the Suburb P data.

(c) Which measure of centre better describes a typical house price in Suburb P? Explain.

(d) Using your answer to (c), in which suburb is a typical house more expensive?

**Question 10**

The daily maximum temperatures (in $^\circ\text{C}$) for one week in two cities are shown.

Hobart: 14, 17, 15, 19, 16, 13, 18

Darwin: 31, 32, 33, 32, 31, 34, 31

(a) Find the mean and range for each city.

(b) Compare the two data sets, referring to both centre and spread.

**Question 11**

A PE class recorded their pulse rates (beats per minute) before and after exercise.

Before: 62, 68, 71, 74, 75, 79, 80, 83

After: 88, 95, 97, 102, 104, 109, 112, 118

(a) Draw a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot of the data, with "Before" on the left and "After" on the right. Use stems 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11, and include a key.

(b) Find the median pulse rate before and after exercise.

(c) Describe the effect of exercise on pulse rate.

**Question 12**

(a) In a positively skewed distribution, which is usually larger: the mean or the median? Explain why.

(b) Find the mean and median of the data set $2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 6, 9, 20$, and check whether your answer to (a) holds.

**Question 13**

Write a data set of 9 whole numbers, each between 1 and 10, that is negatively skewed and has a median of 8. Explain how you know your data set is negatively skewed.

**Question 14**

The ages of people attending two events were recorded. One event was a children's movie session and the other was a pop concert.

| Age group (years) | Event A | Event B |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 9 | 18 | 2 |
| 10 to 19 | 6 | 14 |
| 20 to 29 | 3 | 20 |
| 30 to 39 | 9 | 8 |
| 40 to 49 | 4 | 4 |
| 50 and over | 0 | 2 |

(a) Describe the shape of the distribution for each event.

(b) Which event was the children's movie session? Explain using the shape of the data.

**Question 15**

For each situation, choose the most suitable way to compare the two data sets: a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot, parallel dot plots, or a side-by-side column graph. Give a reason.

(a) Comparing the favourite fruit of Year 7 and Year 9 students.

(b) Comparing the exam marks out of 100 of two classes of 25 students.

(c) Comparing the number of siblings (0 to 5) of students in two classes.

**Question 16**

A shoe shop recorded the sizes of the 10 pairs of shoes sold one morning.

7, 8, 8, 8, 9, 10, 11, 11, 11, 12

(a) Find the mode or modes.

(b) Describe the shape of the distribution.

(c) Find the mean and the median.

(d) Suggest a reason for the shape of this data.

## Section C: Advanced (Questions 17-20)

**Question 17**

Two groups of runners recorded their 5 km times (in minutes). Group A trained with a coach and Group B trained alone.

Group A: 21, 22, 23, 24, 24, 25, 25, 26, 27, 33

Group B: 22, 26, 28, 29, 30, 31, 31, 32, 33, 34

(a) Draw a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot of the data, with Group A on the left and Group B on the right, using stems 2 and 3.

(b) Find the median and range of each group.

(c) Find the mean of each group.

(d) Which group performed better? Use your answers to explain. (Remember that a lower time is better.)

**Question 18**

The scores of 9 students in a quiz were:

8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 24

(a) Find the mean and median.

(b) A tenth student, who sat the quiz late, scored 40. Find the new mean and new median.

(c) Which measure changed more? Explain why.

(d) Describe how adding the score of 40 changes the shape of the distribution.

**Question 19**

The heights (in cm) of 10 Year 3 children and 10 of their parents were measured.

Children: 118, 121, 124, 125, 127, 128, 130, 131, 133, 135

Parents: 158, 162, 165, 168, 170, 172, 175, 178, 180, 186

(a) Combine all 20 heights. Draw a grouped frequency table using the classes 110 to less than 120, 120 to less than 130, and so on, up to 180 to less than 190.

(b) Describe the shape of the combined distribution and explain why it has this shape.

(c) Find the median of the combined data.

(d) Explain why the median is not a good summary of a typical height in this combined data.

**Question 20**

Thirty Year 9 students at each of two schools recorded how many books they read during the holidays.

| Books read | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| School M | 1 | 3 | 6 | 10 | 6 | 3 | 1 |
| School N | 7 | 9 | 6 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 1 |

(a) Describe the shape of each distribution.

(b) Find the mean number of books for each school.

(c) Find the median number of books for each school.

(d) Compare the reading of the two schools, referring to shape and centre.

# Comparing data - Answer Key

**Question 1**

Answer: (a) symmetric (b) positively skewed (c) bi-modal (d) negatively skewed

**Question 2**

Answer: (a) $15$ ($105 \div 7$) (b) $15$ (c) $15$ (d) $16$

**Question 3**

Answer: (a) negatively skewed (b) positively skewed (c) bi-modal (d) symmetric

**Question 4**

Answer: (a) $11$ (b) $45$ years (c) $30$ years ($61 - 31$)

**Question 5**

Answer: (a) $11$ in each class (b) Class A $70$, Class B $62$ (c) Class A $39$ ($91 - 52$), Class B $43$ ($88 - 45$) (d) Class A: its median is higher (70 compared with 62) and its scores are slightly less spread out.

**Question 6**

Answer: (a) both $15$ (b) Ari $6$, Ben $24$ (c) Ari: both have the same mean, but Ari's range is much smaller, so his scores are more consistent.

**Question 7**

Answer: (a) $24$ in each group (b) Group X is positively skewed; Group Y is negatively skewed. (c) Group X $2.5$ hours, Group Y $6$ hours (d) Group Y typically had much more screen time than Group X (median 6 hours compared with 2.5 hours).

**Question 8**

Answer: (a) bi-modal (peaks at 5 to less than 10 and at 20 to less than 25 minutes) (b) For example: there are two groups of people, such as those who had done this type of puzzle before (fast) and those who had not (slow).

**Question 9**

Answer: (a) P: mean \$1 050 000, median \$750 000; Q: mean \$780 000, median \$790 000 (b) positively skewed (one very high price, an outlier) (c) The median, because the one very expensive house pulls the mean up above six of the seven prices. (d) Suburb Q (median \$790 000 compared with \$750 000)

**Question 10**

Answer: (a) Hobart: mean $16^\circ\text{C}$, range $6^\circ\text{C}$; Darwin: mean $32^\circ\text{C}$, range $3^\circ\text{C}$ (b) Darwin was much hotter on average (mean 16 degrees higher) and its temperatures were less spread out (range 3 compared with 6).

**Question 11**

Answer: (a)

| Before | Stem | After |
|---|---|---|
| 8 2 | 6 | |
| 9 5 4 1 | 7 | |
| 3 0 | 8 | 8 |
| | 9 | 5 7 |
| | 10 | 2 4 9 |
| | 11 | 2 8 |

Key: $7 \mid 1$ means 71 beats per minute.

(b) before $74.5$, after $103$ (c) Pulse rates were much higher after exercise (median about 28.5 beats per minute higher) and also more spread out (range 30 compared with 21).

**Question 12**

Answer: (a) The mean, because the few very large values in the tail pull the mean up but do not affect the median much. (b) mean $6$, median $4$; yes, the mean is larger.

**Question 13**

Answer: Many answers are possible, for example $2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9, 10$. Check: 9 whole numbers from 1 to 10, the 5th value in order is 8, and most values are bunched at the high end with a tail of smaller values on the left.

**Question 14**

Answer: (a) Event A is bi-modal (peaks at 0 to 9 and at 30 to 39); Event B is positively skewed (peak at 20 to 29, tail towards older ages). (b) Event A: the two peaks match young children and the adults (parents) who brought them.

**Question 15**

Answer: (a) side-by-side column graph, because the data is categorical (b) back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot, because the data is numerical with many different values (c) parallel dot plots, because there are only a few small whole-number values. (Accept other choices with a sound reason.)

**Question 16**

Answer: (a) $8$ and $11$ (b) bi-modal (c) mean $9.5$, median $9.5$ (d) For example: the shop sells both women's and men's shoes, which tend to be different sizes.

**Question 17**

Answer: (a)

| Group A | Stem | Group B |
|---|---|---|
| 7 6 5 5 4 4 3 2 1 | 2 | 2 6 8 9 |
| 3 | 3 | 0 1 1 2 3 4 |

Key: $2 \mid 4$ means 24 minutes.

(b) Group A: median $24.5$, range $12$; Group B: median $30.5$, range $12$ (c) Group A $25$, Group B $29.6$ (d) Group A performed better: its median and mean times are lower (by 6 minutes and 4.6 minutes), while the ranges are the same.

**Question 18**

Answer: (a) mean $14$, median $13$ (b) mean $16.6$ ($166 \div 10$), median $14$ ($\frac{13 + 15}{2}$) (c) The mean (up $2.6$, compared with up $1$ for the median), because the mean uses the size of every value, so one extreme value pulls it a lot. (d) It adds a long tail to the right, making the data positively skewed.

**Question 19**

Answer: (a)

| Height (cm) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| 110 to less than 120 | 1 |
| 120 to less than 130 | 5 |
| 130 to less than 140 | 4 |
| 140 to less than 150 | 0 |
| 150 to less than 160 | 1 |
| 160 to less than 170 | 3 |
| 170 to less than 180 | 4 |
| 180 to less than 190 | 2 |

(b) bi-modal, with peaks at 120 to less than 130 and 170 to less than 180, because the data combines two different groups (children and adults). (c) $146.5 \text{ cm}$ ($\frac{135 + 158}{2}$) (d) No one has a height near $146.5 \text{ cm}$; it falls in the gap between the two groups, so it describes neither the children nor the parents.

**Question 20**

Answer: (a) School M is symmetric; School N is positively skewed. (b) M $3$ ($90 \div 30$), N $1.8$ ($54 \div 30$) (c) M $3$, N $1$ (d) School M students typically read more books (median 3 compared with 1); School N's data is bunched at low values with a tail of a few keen readers.
